account: Rudy and colleagues describe 17 cases involving 19 patients from seven institutions in which Face2Gene changed clinicians’ testing decisions. The full article reports that clinicians used DeepGestalt, sometimes with Feature Matcher, to analyze photographs and phenotype terms. Cases 1–3 prompted additional testing; Cases 4–17 narrowed the testing approach. In Case 3, a strong KBG match prompted a different ANKRD11 assay after an inconclusive exome, revealing an intragenic deletion. In Case 10, a Cornelia de Lange suggestion led to a panel that included NIPBL, which the originally considered panel omitted. Cases 5–7 illustrate targeted testing after insurance barriers to broader sequencing. The authors selected cases retrospectively from clinicians’ recollections of changed decisions, so the series does not estimate success rates across all consultations. One author was affiliated with FDNA.

ai_role.statement: DeepGestalt supplied ranked facial matches, sometimes combined with phenotype terms through Feature Matcher. Clinicians used those suggestions to add or narrow molecular tests and interpreted the results. The original full-text series documents successful changes in selected cases, including alternative testing after a negative exome, but its retrospective selection does not establish general diagnostic accuracy.

fields.account: Rudy and colleagues describe 17 cases involving 19 patients from seven institutions in which Face2Gene changed clinicians’ testing decisions. The full article reports that clinicians used DeepGestalt, sometimes with Feature Matcher, to analyze photographs and phenotype terms. Cases 1–3 prompted additional testing; Cases 4–17 narrowed the testing approach. In Case 3, a strong KBG match prompted a different ANKRD11 assay after an inconclusive exome, revealing an intragenic deletion. In Case 10, a Cornelia de Lange suggestion led to a panel that included NIPBL, which the originally considered panel omitted. Cases 5–7 illustrate targeted testing after insurance barriers to broader sequencing. The authors selected cases retrospectively from clinicians’ recollections of changed decisions, so the series does not estimate success rates across all consultations. One author was affiliated with FDNA.
